name: PRKDC (SCID)
summary: PRKDC, on chromosome 9, encodes the catalytic subunit of DNA-dependent protein kinase (DNA-PKcs), which repairs double-strand breaks in DNA and is needed for the DNA rearrangement that builds antibodies and T-cell receptors. A five base-pair deletion of TCTCA (c.9478_9482del, p.Asn3160fs*3; g.36395752_36395756del on EquCab3.0; older papers number it c.4675_4679del on another transcript) shifts the reading frame, truncates the protein and removes its kinase activity. Two copies cause severe combined immunodeficiency (SCID): a foal with no adaptive immune system that dies of infection, generally within four to six months. It is recessive; carriers are clinically normal. It is a disease of Arabian and part-Arabian horses. No link between carrier status and sarcoids is established. UC Davis writes the genotypes N/N, N/SCID and SCID/SCID. No effect on coat, build or performance is established.

phenotypes.name: Wild type
phenotypes.description: Two working copies. Nothing is wrong and nothing is passed on.

phenotypes.name: PRKDC (SCID) carrier
phenotypes.description: One copy. The horse is clinically normal and passes the copy to about half its foals. A foal is affected only when both parents pass it on.

phenotypes.name: SCID (no immune system)
phenotypes.description: Two copies. The foal has no working B or T cells and so no adaptive immune system. It suffers repeated or overwhelming infections of every kind - pneumonia, diarrhoea, lethargy, poor growth - and generally does not live beyond about four to six months.
